chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man whose family reckoned that he had died or been killed, so his wife married [another] and his concubine married [another]. So each one of them gave birth from her husband. Then the first husband and the master of the concubine came. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He takes his wife, for he is more rightful with her, and he takes his concubine and her child, or he takes compensation from her price.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a husband returns after his wife and concubine remarried during his presumed death?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the fiqh of 'ghaib' (disappearance) and the rights of a returning husband when his wife and concubine have remarried in good faith during his absence. The Imam’s ruling highlights the distinction between reclaiming the spouse directly versus accepting monetary compensation ('iwad') for the concubine, reflecting the practical legal considerations of marital stability and property rights in Shia jurisprudence. This case study is pivotal for understanding how Shia scholars derive rulings on the validity of subsequent marriages and the financial obligations upon the return of the missing person.
